title: Almost got it but still not right.
text: Almost got it but still not right.. Sadly, my search for the perfect dish drainer continues,as this one won’t work. The main reason is that water pools badly on the drain board and stays there instead of draining into sink. I included a pic in my review. The 2nd reason is because the drain board only drains 1 way so you are forced to set the drainer lengthwise on your counter. And you can’t even push the drainer up against the back wall. The drain board is too narrow and must be aligned with sink. This leaves, on my counter, 3 inches of wasted space between my wall and back of drainer. The expandable drain board is a cool concept. It looks a little wonky but totally works. Love the wine rack and it holds glasses beautifully. I also love the cup rack is over the drain. Gray color is blah.

description: This heavy-duty Expandable Dish Rack from KitchenAid holds up to 11 plates, 6 cups, 4 stemware glasses, plus full-sized pots and pans, and expands from 20.5 inches to 30.9 inches. It features a removable flatware caddy with two compartments, plus a knife block for easy storing. Simply lift and carry to utensil drawer or table. The smart design of this rack features soft, nonslip feet that will protect your countertops while keeping the rack in place. Angled drainboard directs excess water into the sink. The rust-resistant, coated wire also protects dishware.
